releaseNote.summary: Adds attributes.rowSecurity: optional, deny-by-default row rules for the public instance list and GET endpoints. Flows without rowSecurity are unchanged.

rowSecurity.description: A flow declares attributes.rowSecurity.rules (role-keyed row filters in the list-engine filter language, with $.context.Headers / QueryParameters / CurrentUser parameters and the $InstanceStarter / $InstanceBehalfOfStarter identity rules). There is no default: a flow with rowSecurity is deny by default, and 'role X sees everything' is an explicit unfiltered rule; a flow without it is not filtered. A caller sees the OR of the matched static rules' filters plus declared identity rules, ANDed with their own filter; a failed role resolution or any failed parameter yields no rows from that rule and never widens. The rule set is the flow's default version (sys-version-registry pointer) when set, else the latest, read with GetFlowAsync(domain, workflow, null) for instances of every version. Only the public instance list (including groupBy and aggregations) and the single GET endpoint apply it (an excluded instance answers the same 404 as a missing one, before the ETag). Every in-process read is exempt: same-domain GetInstances / GetInstance / GetInstanceData tasks, view content resolution, transitions and direct triggers; a task reading another domain is filtered by that domain's endpoint. A flow lookup failure other than 'no definition' (for example Instance:100052, Instance:100053) never rejects the read: it goes on unfiltered as before, tagged vnext.rowsecurity.outcome=flow-load-failed with warning 20509. GET now performs one cached flow lookup; a flow without rowSecurity answers exactly as before. Requires a gateway that strips or overwrites the role header and every header a rule reads; QueryParameters are client-controlled. Publish warnings (RS-W*) are log-only. A runtime older than this release ignores rowSecurity entirely and serves every row; the only protections on rollback are not rolling back below this release, or blocking/authorizing the list and GET of those flows at the gateway. Requires the runtime version that ships this entry and a vnext-schema release containing workflow.attributes.rowSecurity.

knownIssues.title: rowSecurity filters the public instance list and single GET only; functions, transitions and same-domain tasks serve excluded instances by id, and GET 404 next to data 200 is an existence oracle.
knownIssues.workaround: Do not treat rowSecurity as an access boundary for an instance whose id the caller knows; enforce access to those functions at the gateway (authorize) until instance-addressed coverage ships.
knownIssues.description: rowSecurity filters the public list and single GET endpoints only; state/data/view/schema/master/history/internal functions, transitions, view resolution and same-domain GetInstances/GetInstance/GetInstanceData tasks read excluded instances unfiltered.
